ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All beneficial owners, directors, and senior officers must undergo mandatory screening against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) PEP list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean Ministry of Economy and Finance's domestic sanctions list. Screening must be conducted at onboarding and on a continuous basis using automated systems with manual review. Any match or high-risk jurisdiction triggers enhanced due diligence, including source of funds verification and senior management approval. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Commercial Registry (상업등기) via the Supreme Court of Korea's electronic registration system (인터넷등기소)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Hangul, but may include Latin characters if approved. The name must be registered in the exact form used in the Articles of Association. For foreign names, a phonetic transliteration into Hangul is required. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. The name must not contain prohibited words unless prior ministerial approval is obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Supreme Court of Korea's Registry Division within 14 days of rejection. The appeal must include a written explanation of why the name should be accepted, along with any supporting evidence such as trademark registrations or prior use. The registry will review the appeal and issue a decision within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Seoul Administrative Court within 30 days of the denial.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally not permissible for a company engaged in passive electronic components distribution, as the National Tax Service and commercial banks require a physical presence for verification of business operations, tax registration, and account opening. A serviced office with a physical address and staff may be acceptable, but a pure virtual office without any physical presence is likely to be rejected by tax authorities and banks for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: 1. Physical business signage; 2. Availability of staff during business hours; 3. Access to business records and contracts; 4. Inventory storage or logistics arrangements. Risk: Moderate (30-40% probability of an unannounced inspection within the first year) for a passive distribution company, as the tax authority may verify commercial substance and actual business activity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) of the Republic of Korea

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees for drafting Articles of Association and Board Resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for corporate formation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Sangbeop), Act No. 1000 of January 20, 1962, as amended, Part III, Chapter V (Yuhan Hoesa / Limited Liability Company), Articles 545 through 617; Article 549 (mutatis mutandis application of stock company provisions); Commercial Registration Rules of the Supreme Court; Foreign Investment Promotion Act (if non-resident members).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Section, Registration Division, Civil Affairs Office of the district court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Seoul Central District Court), operating through the Supreme Court InterNet Commercial Registration System.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Commercial Registration of a Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company) under the Commercial Registration Rules, accompanied by notarized Articles of Incorporation, payment delivery receipts, specimen of corporate seal, and the required schedules of members and investments.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act imposes no minimum paid-in capital for a Yuhan Hoesa; there is no statutory blocked escrow account. The Articles of Incorporation must state the total amount of each member contribution and the monetary amount per contribution unit on an equal basis. Cash contributions must be deposited into a domestic bank account established in the proposed corporate name before the registration filing, and the bank's contribution receipt must be submitted to the registry. In-kind contributions require an independent valuation certificate and a member resolution. For a representative capital base of KRW 100,000,000, the aggregate court and tax costs are approximately USD 370.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea as a Yuhan Hoesa, with the corporate name and Articles of Incorporation presented to this meeting, be and it is hereby adopted, ratified and approved in all respects. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the subscriptions and contributions to the paid-in capital set forth in the contribution ledger and subscription statements, showing each member's name, contribution units, amount contributed and the aggregate paid-in capital, be and they are hereby accepted by the Company; that the capital contributions have been actually received by the Company through deposit into the Company's pre-registration account at [Bank Name] and credited to the capital account of the Company; and that the representative director is authorized to execute and deliver contribution receipts, unit certificates and any related documents to each member. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company at [Registered Office Address] in the Republic of Korea is hereby adopted as the statutory seat, registered office and legal address of the Company for all purposes; that the representative director shall file the necessary registration application with the competent district court registry and shall publish or give notice as required by the Articles of Incorporation; and that the corporate seal adopted at this meeting shall be the official seal of the Company. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the following statutory officers are hereby appointed to hold office from the date of this resolution until successors are duly elected and qualified: [Name] as Representative Director; [Name] as Internal Director; [Name] as Auditor or Audit Committeeman if required under the Articles; each such officer shall exercise the powers and perform the duties imposed by the Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer are hereby jointly and severally authorized to open, maintain, operate and close banking accounts at [Bank Name] in the name of the Company, to receive SWIFT wire transfers and to apply for credit lines and trade facilities in connection with the distribution and inventory management of passive electronic components, and that any one of such officers may sign checks, payment orders and banking instructions as required by the bank. RESOLVED, FINALLY, that all acts of the incorporators, directors, officers, counsel and agents in connection with the incorporation, capital formation, registration, corporate seal filing, business registration, lease of premises, and procurement of ancillary licenses or insurance are hereby approved, ratified and confirmed in their entirety.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Legal Due Diligence and Name and Address Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court InterNet Commercial Registration System and the local district court registry; Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO) for trademark conflicts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage licensed Korean counsel to conduct due diligence on each incorporator, proposed director and statutory auditor. Verify the proposed Korean and romanized company name against the Supreme Court commercial registration database and KIPO trademark register. Confirm that the intended registered office address physically exists and is capable of receiving commercial registration service, and that the lease does not prohibit corporate use. Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation containing all mandatory clauses under the Commercial Act: corporate name, business purpose for ISIC 4652 (distribution and inventory of excess multilayer ceramic capacitors and resistors), registered office address, total number of contribution units, amount per contribution unit, aggregate paid-in capital, method of giving public notice, names and contribution amounts of each member, and the appointment of directors and auditor. Execute a power of attorney in favor of the filing counsel for all subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of all incorporators and directors
Proposed Korean and English company names
Registered office lease agreement or address consent letter
Draft Articles of Incorporation prepared in Korean
Power of attorney for filing attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected or a trademark conflict is identified, submit three alternate names and re-run the verification; if a member or officer is found disqualified, replace that person before signing the Articles, and if the registered office is unsuitable, change the address and obtain a new consent letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Deposit of Paid-In Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public in the district of the registered office; licensed Korean bank authorized to provide corporate pre-registration accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Schedule and attend the notarization of the Articles of Incorporation. All founders must appear in person or through an attorney holding a notarized power of attorney bearing the founder's true signature and seal. The notary must certify that the Articles are prepared in the Korean language and comply with the mandatory content requirements for a Yuhan Hoesa. After notarization, open a temporary account in the name of the proposed company and deposit the full cash contributions from each member before the commercial registration application is submitted. Obtain a bank certificate of deposit or contribution receipt stating the depositor, proposed company name, and amount. For any in-kind contribution, obtain a professional valuation report and attach the members' written resolution approving the value. All contribution evidence must be held in the registration file.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Notarized power of attorney for each founder appearing by proxy
Government-issued IDs for each founder and officer
Bank deposit certificate or transfer receipt for capital contribution
Professional valuation report for in-kind contribution, if any
Member resolution approving in-kind contribution value, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to any clause, revise the Articles by unanimous member written consent and re-notarize; if the bank delays opening the pre-registration account, use an alternative licensed bank and provide updated deposit receipts before filing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; operational electronic portals: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr) for business registration, corporate income tax, VAT, e-Tax Invoice transmission; Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr) for export customs clearance and export declaration records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Korean Yuhan Hoesa domestic entity: (1) incorporate the Yuhan Hoesa and procure the corporate seal certificate and register with the Commercial Registry; (2) file the Application for Business Registration with the competent district tax office through HomeTax or the local tax office; (3) receive the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which functions as the entity's Corporate Taxpayer Identification Number, VAT registration number, and e-Tax Invoice issuer ID; (4) obtain the Korea Customs Service exporter clearance identifier by registering the business number in UNI-PASS, enabling electronic filing of export declarations; (5) register bank account details with a Korean foreign-exchange bank for settlement of export proceeds; (6) if the Korean entity is not yet formed and a foreign non-resident enterprise is supplying goods or services into Korea directly, the non-resident enterprise must appoint a Korean tax representative, submit the foreign registration certificate, articles of incorporation or equivalent, passport or corporate identity documents, a completed application through HomeTax, and obtain a foreign resident business registration number for VAT purposes. The Yuhan Hoesa itself, being locally incorporated, follows the domestic registration route regardless of foreign ownership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Korean Corporate Tax Act does not provide a check-the-box or other domestic entity classification election. A Yuhan Hoesa is a Korean domestic corporation taxed at entity level on worldwide income; no hybrid mismatch election exists. Foreign classification of the entity under a treaty jurisdiction does not override Korean domestic entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold applies to a Korean domestic legal entity; VAT registration is mandatory at business commencement. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean establishment, any VAT-taxable supply in Korea creates a mandatory registration obligation; the simplified taxpayer threshold available to Korean micro-entrepreneurs is not available to foreign legal entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT-registered businesses must issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax electronic tax invoice system for supplies to other businesses. The e-Tax Invoice data is transmitted to HomeTax and centrally matched by the NTS; large ERP systems may transmit via NTS API or EDI interfaces. Korea does not operate a pre-clearance digital stamp model: the anti-fraud system relies on mandatory issuance and transmission deadlines, unique e-Tax Invoice serial numbers, real-time declaration comparison of sales and purchase ledger information, and penalty surcharges for non-issuance, late issuance, or false issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Korean Value Added Tax Act, exported goods are zero-rated where the seller exports to a foreign buyer, the goods are cleared through Korea Customs Service export declaration, title and risk transfer overseas, and payment is received from a non-resident in foreign currency. The zero-rated transaction does not bear output VAT, and creditable input VAT from related purchases is refundable by the National Tax Service. For the current passive electronic component distribution activity, each inventory sale to a non-Korean customer must be physically exported from Korea and supported by the documentation bundle below; sales of the same inventory to a Korean domestic customer are subject to standard 10% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Customs Declaration (UNI-PASS export clearance record)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (or multimodal transport document) evidencing physical dispatch from Korea to the foreign consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Korean Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate evidencing receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Commercial invoice, packing list, and HS classification/weight/value records matching the export declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service jointly audit zero-rating substantiation. If any mandatory document is missing, inconsistent, or the export proceeds are not collected through Korean banking channels within the 180-day deadline, the zero-rating is retrospectively disallowed; the taxpayer is assessed 10% VAT on the affected supply, plus penalty surcharges under the Framework Act for National Taxes (generally 10% to 40% of the underpaid VAT, with higher surcharges for intentional concealment). False or forged export declarations can trigger criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, customs export penalties, seizure or denial of exporter privileges, and clawback of any VAT refund with interest. Re-importation or diversion of zero-rated goods into Korean domestic commerce also re-exposes the goods to import duty and VAT.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won is fully convertible for current account transactions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; capital account transactions are liberalized but subject to reporting requirements and a real-demand identity. Export proceeds must be collected within one year but there is no mandatory surrender or conversion ratio; proceeds can be retained in foreign currency settlement accounts at a domestic licensed foreign exchange bank. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted provided the remitting bank verifies the prior filing of the foreign investment report, confirms absence of Korean tax arrears, and receives a certified copy of the distribution resolution. Any capital outflow that lacks a genuine underlying trade or investment contract may be recharacterized as disguised capital flight and denied by the bank. The MOEF and BOK jointly restrict offshore KRW liquidity, and non-resident access to onshore won is limited to legitimate trade-invoiced amounts. A corporate treasurer must therefore maintain a complete documentary trail of each transaction, carefully separate current account and capital account flows, and report all FX position changes in the Foreign Exchange Information Reporting System (FEIRS) to avoid administrative penalties and reputational damage. Central bank oversight is active, with strict audit powers exercised through the Bank of Korea's examination functions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 16 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, exporters must receive export proceeds within one year from the date of export declaration; extensions require MOEF approval. There is no mandatory conversion into KRW and no surrender ratio; exporters may retain funds at a domestic authorized foreign exchange bank in foreign currency, but they must submit a settlement receipt report to the bank and preserve trade documentation for five years. Failure to collect proceeds within the statutory timeline or to report the settlement constitutes an administrative violation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment Deposit) and Basic Operational Koreana Won Onshore Settlement Account
Foreign Exchange Settlement Account with separate KRW operating account for MLCC/Resistor distribution activities
Basic Operational Currency Account plus a documentary Letter of Credit margin and collections account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs are not permitted to provide foreign-exchange-linked deposit, escrow, or settlement services to Korean resident entities. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act confers FX banking powers exclusively on licenced domestic banks, and EMIs holding only e-money licenses in their host country cannot clear KRW or hold customer funds for Korean corporations. A fintech EMI may function solely as an introducing agent or software technology vendor to a domestic bank, never as an independent treasury rail. Therefore, cross-border treasury liquidity must be built on Tier-1 Korean bank core custody and Swift-based clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed foreign-owned LLC, the statutory representative and at least one authorized signatory must appear in person at a domestic bank branch to complete risk-based due diligence and biometric verification. Remote opening using a consular proxy or a virtual notary is not generally accepted for capital escrow or FX settlement accounts. Some Tier-1 banks allow a single representative visit if all other directors provide notarized and apostilled powers of attorney, certified passport copies, and a full corporate registry extract. In all cases the bank will conduct a live interview covering beneficial ownership, source of funds, trade counterparties, and expected transaction volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Significant non-resident ownership without a clear source-of-funds trail for the initial equity or subordinated loan
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a notarized board resolution approving the capital injection; for each qualifying UBO supply six months of personal bank statements, certified passport pages, a written source-of-wealth declaration, and an independent auditor's confirmation that funds do not originate from shell or high-risk crypto chains.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered-agent address and a passive component distribution profile that may be mischaracterized as a shelf company with no operational substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a physical office lease or a public virtual office registration, genuine inventory contracts from suppliers and wholesale customers, warehouse storage agreements, Korea Customs Service import VAT filings on MLCCs and resistors, and a rolling 12-month business plan demonstrating operating headcount and logistics flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlement routing through third-party intermediary accounts or a failure to show a complete contractual chain for trade payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide end-to-end contracts from original manufacturer to end customer, original invoices, packing lists, bills of lading and customs declarations, and enforce a written policy absolutely prohibiting cash settlements and requiring pre-approval for any sub-contracting entity that receives funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions or dual-use exposure embedded in passive electronic components used by military or industrial buyers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver an internal export-control screening policy, third-party denied-party and sanctions list checks, end-user certificates for each customer, and a formal quarantine procedure for suspicious orders; obtain a bank-side advisory opinion from the trade compliance committee before opening the account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder loans are routed through a domestic authorized foreign exchange bank using the Foreign Exchange Information Reporting System (FEIRS). The investor must first submit a capital transaction report to the bank or MOEF covering the amount and purpose code (e.g., foreign direct investment code 701200 for a stake in a Korean entity). The funds are credited to a dedicated foreign investment deposit account, then converted into won or retained in foreign currency in a basic operational account. Capital verification is accomplished by presenting the bank's certificate of registration, a company registry application, and evidence of the deposit balance to the Korean court registry. All inward remittances must include a witness-specific purpose category in SWIFT field 70 to avoid misclassification and treasury delays.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for passive electronic components are cleared primarily through SWIFT MT103 for open-account payments, import letters of credit through SWIFT MT700 for deferred or sight payment arrangements, and documentary collections with draft instructions. For LC settlements, the Korean bank issues the LC under an accepted import declaration from Korea Customs Service; the beneficiary bank presents documents and the issuing bank remits cover via MT202/MT103. The treasury must maintain full documentary audit trails for each MT103 remittance, matching invoices, packing slips, and customs declarations, and must process all outbound transfers before the value date to respect Korean bank business cut-offs for KRW interbank clearing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward foreign exchange contracts against participant banks, subject to the real-demand principle and maximum one-year tenor for trade-backed positions
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referenced to the Korean won for offshore settlement where physical KRW delivery is prohibited or operationally impractical
Cross-currency swaps for balance sheet matching of long-term foreign capital and asset exposures, with deals restricted to commercial banks licenced by the MOEF and Bank of Korea

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax final return and self-assessment under Article 60 of the Corporate Income Tax Act, including audited or reviewed financial statements when required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service via HomeTax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months from the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year; a one-month extension is available for foreign-currency or foreign-affiliated documentation circumstances, and any further extension only under a lawful pre-approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unreported income penalty of 20% of unpaid tax, increasing to 40% for concealment or fraud; under-reported income penalty of 10% of omitted tax; statutory delinquency interest currently calculated at approximately 0.022% per day from the original due date; prolonged non-payment or disappearance of the business can trigger NTS business registration closure, seizure of bank accounts and inventory, and administrative dissolution-equivalent enforcement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (top national marginal rate; plus 10% local income tax surtax, resulting in a combined top marginal rate of 26.4%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME preferential 9% rate on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; foreign-investment tax holiday in free economic zones (100% exemption for 5 years and 50% reduction for 2 years); R&D expense tax credits up to 30%; technology income transfer exemption and special tax incentives under the Special Taxation Act for reshoring/distribution ventures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Corporate Tax Act Article 60) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing system (www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year corporation, by March 31 of the following year (extendable by up to 1 month on application, and further for corporations with statutory external audit requirements)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business Registration Number, corporate name, tax office code, representative director, and place of effective management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the full business registration data of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa; non-resident ownership does not exempt the entity from domestic filing, and the responsible National Tax Service regional office is determined by the registered place of management.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and statement of comprehensive income based on K-IFRS or Korean GAAP, showing sales, cost of sales, and operating expenses for the electronic components distribution business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report passive electronic component inventory trading as ordinary sales revenue and cost of inventory sold; ensure intercompany purchases/sales values match transfer pricing documentation and customs declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting net income to taxable income by adding back non-deductible expenses and applying statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for non-deductible accruals, inventory write-downs, entertainment expenses in excess of limits, and any transfer pricing secondary adjustments; all foreign-parent head office expense allocations must be substantiated with OECD-compliant supporting data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of corporate income tax at progressive brackets on the adjusted tax base, plus local income tax surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion; calculate local income tax of 10% on the computed national corporate income tax and report as a separate line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 40 - Foreign Tax Credit and Non-Resident Disclosure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of foreign income, foreign source taxes paid, foreign tax credit claimed, and details of foreign shareholder holdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all foreign shareholders with percentage ownership, jurisdiction of residence, and functional role; attach tax residency certificates for any treaty rate claimed on dividend remittances; verify beneficial ownership to prevent treaty shopping denial.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing triggers a 20% surcharge on the unpaid tax, or 40% where there is gross negligence or fraudulent intention, under the Framework Act on National Taxes; subsequent daily late-payment interest accrues at 0.022% per day. Criminal tax evasion is punishable under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act by imprisonment with labor for up to 2 years or a fine equal to three times the evaded tax, or both.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% (plus 10% local income tax surtax on the withholding amount, resulting in effective tax of 22%)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced rate under a Double Tax Treaty, the foreign shareholder must provide a Tax Residency Certificate issued by its country of residence, complete the official application for non-resident tax exemption/reduction, state the treaty article relied on, and prove beneficial ownership of the Korean-source dividend. The Korean withholding agent must submit this package to the National Tax Service before or at the time of remittance; if excess tax was withheld, a refund claim must be filed within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalty and interest payments to non-residents is 20% each (plus 2% local surtax for a total 22%). Under many Korean treaties, interest and royalties may be reduced to 0%-15% for beneficial owners, and certain government-related or financial-entity interest can be exempt; treaty relief requires a substance-based beneficial ownership analysis.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5,000,000,000 in aggregate international related-party transactions in the preceding fiscal year, combined with annual total revenue exceeding KRW 50,000,000,000, triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation and submission with the annual corporate tax return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not have a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations law, but substance-over-form, beneficial ownership, and the statutory general anti-abuse rule require the Korean LLC to perform actual core income-generating activities (CIGA) such as procurement, inventory logistics for MLCC and resistor distribution, invoicing, and management decisions within Korea. A mailbox or conduit arrangement with no local employees, assets, or decision-making will not qualify for treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately failing to report Korean-source revenues from passive electronic component sales, submitting false zero returns, or creating fictitious intercompany invoices to shift profits offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, intentional tax evasion carries imprisonment with labor for up to 2 years or a fine up to three times the evaded tax; additionally the Framework Act on National Taxes imposes a 40% fraud penalty plus daily late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who ordered or knowingly approved the sham filing lose the corporate veil shield and are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax, penalties, and interest; they may also be blacklisted by the National Tax Service, subject to travel bans, and face criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold on Outbound Dividends and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends, interest, or royalties to the foreign shareholder without deducting the 20% statutory withholding tax and remitting it to the National Tax Service, while also failing to document treaty relief eligibility.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent is personally liable for the unwithheld tax, plus an additional tax under the withholding provisions and daily late-payment interest; criminal penalties apply for intentional failure to collect and pay national taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for treasury and disbursements are jointly liable for the unpaid withholding tax and surcharges; in cases of deliberate diversion, they face asset seizure, exit bans, and prosecution as co-perpetrators of tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Shopping and Economic Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Korean Yuhan Hoesa as a mere conduit to hold title to passive electronic inventory, route payments from suppliers to a related foreign distributor, and claim treaty-reduced withholding without engaging in actual distribution activities, having real employees, or maintaining any commercial substance in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority can deny treaty benefits, re-characterise the transaction under the statutory anti-abuse rule, reassess income at full statutory rates, impose a 40% unfaithful return penalty, and refer the matter for criminal investigation under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who structured the conduit may face civil restitution of all underpaid taxes and penalties, pierce-the-veil personal liability as persons responsible for management, blacklisting and travel restrictions, and criminal sanctions for aiding tax evasion if they are shown to have directed the artificial arrangement.
